newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firm, seen scoring new gains.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firm, seen scoring new gains.

text.p: Croatian stocks were stable to higher on Thursday in quiet trade and traders said they could score new gains with the buying lull coming to an end.
But market activity was likely to remain subdued this week in post-holiday mood.
"Trading will go on quietly tomorrow," said one trader with a large market share.
He said most issues, led by drugs firm Pliva forging ahead after its shares were split at 37 for one, would probably start a steady recovery soon.
"Pliva is on the rise now and it will attract more and more small investors who could not afford to buy its expensive stock before," the trader added.
After the New Year split, Pliva was the day's most active issue with 2,701 units sold, firming 3.86 percent to 393 kuna -- two down from the intraday high and its all-time record.
It ended last year at 14,000 kuna after firming on Tuesday. Its GDRs, now representing 1/5 of each share, traded at $14.75/85 on the London Stock Exchange on Thursday.
Five other stocks out of a total of 10 traded also bounced up and four remained stable.
Top gainer was hotelier Istraturist, up 7.69 percent to 140 kuna from a fortnight ago with 50 shares sold.
Others included confectioner Kras and Podravka food concern which rose 13 and five kuna respectively on volume of 143 and 917 shares.
Another fully-listed issue, Zagrebacka Banka, regained 20 kuna or 1.87 percent to 1,080 kuna with only 10 shares changing hands. Its 1/10 GDRs rose to $20.69 each on Seaq.
Zagrebacka's rarely traded E-series preference stock was steady at 450 kuna on a volume of 606 units.
